title: Normalized section specialization for ordinary etale dualizing complexes over a Noetherian base
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $S,V$ be Noetherian schemes (admitting finite affine open covers by spectra of Noetherian rings) on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $g:V\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed section, with ideal $\mathcal I$, and assume it is regular of codimension $d$: locally $\mathcal I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, where multiplication by $x_i$ is injective on $\mathcal O_V/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})$ for each $i$, and the quotient by all $x_i$ is $\mathcal O_S$. Its conormal sheaf $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of rank $d$; put $\pi:N=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)\to S$ with zero section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Define $D=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$, where $\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$ is the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and all $a/t$ for local sections $a\in\mathcal I$. Write $\widetilde g:D\to\mathbf A^1_S$ for its structural map [def-sbc-affine-space], and $\widetilde s:\mathbf A^1_S\to D$ for the section induced by $s^*\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal O_S$, $t\mapsto t$, and $\mathcal I/t\mapsto0$. Assume $g$, $\pi$, and $\widetilde g$ are compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Use only the ordinary unbounded derived categories of etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and put $\omega_h=h^\times A_{\operatorname{target}(h)}$ using the ordinary compact-support adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. All inverse images are the exact constant-coefficient inverse images, extended to derived categories [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

The scheme $D$ is Noetherian, $\widetilde g$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$, and its pairs with section over $t=1$ and $t=0$ are canonically $(g,s)$ and $(\pi,z)$. Put $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, $C=s^*\omega_g$, and $F=\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}$. The complexes $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$ are locally constant sheaves of free rank-one $A$-modules. Under the fibre identifications supplied by the canonical exceptional base-change maps [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], there is a unique isomorphism
$$\kappa_{g,s}:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$$
whose restriction at $t=1$ is $1_C$. In particular
$$\delta_{g,s}=(i_0^*\kappa_{g,s})^{-1}:s^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi,$$
where $i_0:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ is $t=0$. For any morphism $S'\to S$ of Noetherian schemes for which the three base-changed maps are compactifiable, pullback carries $\kappa_{g,s}$ and $\delta_{g,s}$ to the respective normalized comparisons for the base-changed section, under the canonical exceptional base-change identifications.

proof.text: Choose affine open neighbourhoods $S_i$ of points of $S$ and neighbourhoods $U_i$ of $s(S_i)$ in $V_i=V\times_SS_i$. The pointwise smooth normal form gives $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ etale; its relative dimension is $d$ because $g$ has that relative dimension. Subtract from each coordinate its value on $s$ so that $e_is=0$. These choices can be made with $S_i$ and $U_i$ affine: after choosing an affine neighbourhood of $s(b)$, shrink the base to an affine principal neighbourhood contained in its inverse image under $s$. In particular $e_i$ is separated (its source is affine). Its inverse image $P_i=e_i^{-1}(0)$ is separated etale over $S_i$, by base change. Its section $s$ is an open-and-closed immersion by the etale-section lemma. Since $P_i$ is closed in $U_i$, the complementary component $P_i\setminus s(S_i)$ is closed in $U_i$; remove it. If necessary choose affine neighbourhoods again and shrink the base as just described. We obtain an open cover of $S$ with separated finite-type etale charts $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ for which the centre square is Cartesian. On an affine chart write $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$. Then $I=JB$, $B/I=R$, and $B$ is flat over $P$ (etale implies flat, with the affine flatness criterion). No isomorphism $U_i=\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ is asserted.

proof.text:
Here is the flat Rees calculation, keeping the chart algebra $B$. Exactness of tensoring with the flat $P$-module $B$ identifies $B\otimes_PJ^m$ with its image $J^mB=I^m$ in $B$, and identifies $B\otimes_P(J^m/J^{m+1})$ with $I^m/I^{m+1}$, for every $m\geq0$. The extended Rees algebra has Laurent degree pieces $P t^k$ for $k\geq0$ and $J^m t^{-m}$ for $m>0$. Tensor these pieces and their inclusions in $P[t,t^{-1}]$; the images are exactly the corresponding pieces of $B[t,I/t]$, and multiplication is multiplication of the coefficients. Consequently
$$B[t,I/t]\cong B\otimes_P P[t,J/t]\cong B\otimes_{R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]}R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d],\qquad x_j\mapsto tu_j.$$
The second isomorphism is checked on monomials: $x^\alpha t^k$ with $k\geq-|\alpha|$ corresponds to $u^\alpha t^{k+|\alpha|}$. Also the canonical map $\operatorname{Sym}_{B/I}(I/I^2)\to\bigoplus_{m\geq0}I^m/I^{m+1}$ is an isomorphism: tensor the homogeneous monomial bases for $J^m/J^{m+1}$, using $B\otimes_P R=B/I=R$. It sends $[x_j]$ to the degree-one class of $x_j$. These canonical maps agree on overlaps, so this proves the global $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I}\mathcal O_V\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)$. This is an explicit consequence of flat tensor exactness and monomial multiplication, rather than an additional Rees or regular-immersion lemma.

source.place: Local construction, first paragraph, algebra behind etale base change of the deformation; Stacks 00HD/lemma-flat; compare 0805/lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up

proof.text: The displayed algebra makes $D_{U_i}$ the base change of the etale chart $e_i$ along $(u,t)\mapsto(tu,t)$, hence gives a separated etale morphism $\widetilde e_i:D_{U_i}\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$. It sends the deformed section to the zero section. For the full extended Rees algebra, quotient by $t$ has degree-$m$ part $I^m/I^{m+1}$, so Step 2 identifies the zero fibre globally with $N=\operatorname{Spec}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)$ and the section with $z$. Inverting $t$ gives $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$; evaluation at $t=1$ gives $V$ and $s$. The opens $D_{U_i}$ cover the whole zero fibre because their images cover the centre in $V$; together with $D[t^{-1}]=V\times_S\mathbf G_{m,S}$ they cover $D$. The affine projections are smooth of dimension $d$, their etale pullbacks have the same dimension by smooth permanence, and the punctured chart is the base change of $g$. Thus $\widetilde g$ is smooth of dimension $d$. Every ideal in a Noetherian affine coordinate ring is finitely generated, so the extended Rees algebra is generated by $t$ and finitely many $f_j/t$. This makes $D\to V$ finite type, and $D$ is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian lemma. The map $D\to V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S$ is affine and separated: on affine charts its diagonal is cut out by the kernel of the surjective multiplication homomorphism $Q\otimes_{B[t]}Q\to Q$. Its composite with the separated base change $V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ is separated: the diagonal factors through $D\times_{V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S}D$, which is a closed subscheme of $D\times_{\mathbf A^1_S}D$ by pulling back the diagonal of $g$. P2 Lean realization (2026-10-19): geometry reuses Scheme.Hom.smoothOfRelativeDimension_deformationSpaceProj, the existing separated and quasi-compact instances, the two canonical fibre squares and their section identities. LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace give Noetherianity. For the final conormal clauses, use the canonical affine identifications already computed in Step 2, with the conormal algebra and its symmetric comparison as specified in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. The degree-one classes of the $x_j$ form a basis of $I/I^2$ of length $d$, and the canonical map from its symmetric algebra to the associated graded sends this basis to the same degree-one generators. Under Step 2's polynomial identifications this map is the identity, hence is invertible. These canonical comparisons agree on overlaps, giving the asserted locally free rank and global isomorphism. This includes $d=0$ (the empty basis and degree-zero algebra) and the empty base. The Lean helper regularNormalBundle packages this local calculation; the global pro-etale purity and constructible six-functor conventions are not inputs to it.

proof.text:
The algebra and normal-bundle identifications commute even with nonflat base change $S'\to S$. Check over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq S'\times_SS_i$. Put $P'=R'[x]$, $B'=B\otimes_RR'$ and $I'=JB'$. The chart $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}P'$ is etale by base change, hence flat, and $B'/I'=R'$. Applying the calculation of Step 2 to this chart gives
$$B[t,I/t]\otimes_RR'\cong B'\otimes_{P'}R'[t,u]\cong B'[t,I'/t].$$
The map here is the canonical map sending $b$ to $b\otimes1$, $t$ to $t$, and $x_j/t$ to $x'_j/t$. Similarly, $[x_j]\mapsto[x'_j]$ identifies the base change of $I/I^2$ with $I'/I'^2$ and identifies their symmetric algebras. Thus it respects both sections, evaluation at $1$, and the associated-graded map at $0$. On $t\ne0$ the assertion is the elementary tensor identity for $B[t,t^{-1}]$. These equalities glue (all the homomorphisms were canonical), giving the base-changed deformation and normal bundle. In particular the regular coordinates and their regular-sequence property survive this base change, since $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ form a regular sequence in $R'[x]$ and flat tensor exactness preserves the successive injections. The base-changed data again satisfy the hypotheses of the statement over $S'$: $\ell$ is invertible on $S'$ because it is on $S$; $g':V'=V\times_SS'\to S'$ is separated and of finite type by separated finite-type base change, and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by smooth permanence (1), so $V'$ is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian lemma; and $s'=s\times_SS'$ is a section of $g'$ which is the base change of the closed immersion $s$ along $V'\to V$ (since $S\times_VV'=S\times_SS'=S'$), hence a closed immersion. On the charts above, which cover $s'(S')$, its ideal is $I'=JB'$. Lean implementation of baseChange_geometry reuses the existing Scheme.Hom.exists_isPushout_extendedReesAlgebraMap_baseChange for these local algebra identities, and Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPullback_deformationSpaceMap_proj to obtain the Cartesian square for the stipulated deformationMap. The normalMap is the pullback lift already defined in the statement module. Its two projection identities, horizontal pasting of the zero-fibre squares, and pullback cancellation prove its Cartesian property. Pullback hom_ext and the canonical section identities prove the zero-section compatibility. Closed immersion and quasi-compactness follow by base change; no chosen identification of a normal bundle is needed for these clauses.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary-etale smooth tensor theorem to $g$, $\pi$, and $\widetilde g$. The ring $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ is finite and killed by $\ell^n$, which is invertible on every scheme here. These three maps are separated, smooth of dimension $d$, and compactifiable by the statement; Step 3 has verified the remaining hypotheses for $\widetilde g$. The bases and sources are Noetherian (for affine space and the vector bundle use the finite-type Noetherian lemma). Thus $\omega_h[-2d]$ is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf. Exact inverse image preserves this property, so $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$ are sheaves of the claimed kind. The adjoints and the complexes are those on the entire ordinary unbounded etale derived categories, as required; no pro-etale or coefficient-completion comparison is used. Lean implementation reuses AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_dualizingComplex_iso_and_tensor, the existing source interface underlying thm-asd-smooth-tensor. Pull back its locally constant sheaf along the section and use the single-complex and shift compositors. Refine the local-constancy cover by pairs consisting of a cover member and one of its points. An algebraic-closure point on each nonempty member, and the geometric stalk isomorphism, identify its constant coefficient module with A. This also treats the empty base without a nonemptiness assumption. The invertible exponent hypothesis is assembled from stalkwise invertibility by isUnit_of_isUnit_germ.

source.place: Opening paragraph: shifted lisse lines, with ordinary-etale smooth tensor theorem

proof.text:
Let $i_r:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ be $t=r$, for $r=0,1$. The canonical exceptional base-change maps for $\widetilde g$ and $i_r$, pulled to the section and using Step 3, give
$$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C,\qquad \eta:i_0^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi.$$
These are the specified fibre identifications, not chosen orientations. The base-change theorem applies because the fibre maps are $g$ and $\pi$, both compactifiable, and all schemes are Noetherian. Inverse image is exact, so it commutes with the common shift and is the termwise pullback used here. Lean implementation uses the existing isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension and isIso_dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap_iff. Pullback and composition preserve isomorphisms, so the defined sectionMap, atOne and atZero are isomorphisms.

source.place: Opening paragraph: the fibre restrictions at t=1 and t=0

proof.text: Construct the local comparison using etale locality, rather than identifying an etale chart with affine space. All the maps $U_i\to S_i$, $D_{U_i}\to\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$, the two affine-space projections, the chart maps $e_i,\widetilde e_i$, and the open inclusions into $V_i,D_i$ are separated of finite type between Noetherian schemes. For the chart maps, both source and target are affine, so their locally finite-presentation etale maps are quasi-compact and hence finite type; the composites through affine space are finite type as well. For an open inclusion, the inverse image of an affine target open is an open subscheme of its Noetherian source, hence quasi-compact by the cited open-subscheme lemma; locally the inclusion is an isomorphism, so it is finite type. Open inclusions are etale since they are locally identity maps. The source opens are Noetherian. Every Noetherian target is quasi-compact by its finite affine cover, and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact by the open-subscheme lemma, so it is quasi-separated. Nagata therefore supplies compactifications for every required chart composite.

source.place: Local construction, second and third paragraphs: etale pullback of the standard pair and normalization at t=1

proof.text: Etale/open locality of the ordinary compact-support right adjoint first identifies $\omega_{g_i}|_{U_i}$ with $\omega_{g_i|_{U_i}}$, and then with $e_i^*\omega_{p_d}$, since $g_i|_{U_i}=p_de_i$. It gives the same two identifications for the deformation chart, with $\widetilde e_i$ in place of $e_i$. The ordinary affine-space adjunction and uniqueness of right adjoints identify $\omega_{p_d}$ with $A(d)[2d]$ on $\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$, and the corresponding dualizing object over $\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$ with $A(d)[2d]$ there. Pull these identifications to the two sections. Pullback of finite-coefficient etale Tate sheaves identifies both results with the pullback of the same $A_{S_i}(d)[2d]$. Smooth base change for $S_i\to S$ identifies them with $C|_{S_i}$ and $F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$, respectively. This produces an isomorphism $\lambda_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}\to a_i^*(C|_{S_i})$. If $h_i=(i_1^*\lambda_i)\theta_i^{-1}$, replace $\lambda_i$ by $a_i^*(h_i^{-1})\lambda_i$. Its restriction at $1$ is exactly $\theta_i$. This normalization does not presume compatibility of any chosen affine orientation with the fibre map.

source.place: Local construction, second and third paragraphs: etale pullback of the standard pair and normalization at t=1

proof.text: To pass from derived maps to sheaf maps, shift by $[-2d]$ and apply full faithfulness of the degree-zero single-complex functor to the rank-one sheaves of Step 5. This identifies each derived local comparison and its inverse with actual sheaf morphisms and respects their compositions. On $S_i\cap S_j$, the ratio $\lambda_j\lambda_i^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $a^*C[-2d]$. Its scalar is intrinsic: in a local basis it is multiplication by $u\in A^\times$, and a different basis changes this to $vuv^{-1}=u$ since $A$ is commutative. Pull it to a geometric fibre $\mathbf A^1_{\Omega}$, where $a^*C[-2d]$ is the constant free rank-one module obtained from its fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The ring $\Omega[t]$ is a domain, so $(0)$ is prime and its closure in the spectrum is the whole spectrum; the spectrum is irreducible, hence connected. The constant-sheaf section lemma implies that $u$ is constant on this fibre. Its value at $t=1$ is $1$ by normalization, so the ratio is the identity on every geometric fibre. It is therefore the identity on every geometric stalk. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks give equality of the sheaf maps: apply them to the image of their difference, which has all stalks zero. This proves agreement on every overlap and proves that any two global normalized comparisons agree, by the identical ratio argument.

source.place: Gluing, first paragraph: sheaf realization and the connected geometric-fibre argument

proof.text:
Apply sheaf-Hom gluing to the normalized sheaf maps of Step 9 on the cover $\{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}\to\mathbf A^1_S\}$. Their inverse maps also agree and glue, so the resulting sheaf morphism is an isomorphism. Shift back to obtain $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C$. It restricts to $\theta$ at $1$, and Step 9 gives the asserted uniqueness. At $0$, the actual map from $C$ to $z^*\omega_\pi$ is
$$\delta=\eta\circ(i_0^*\kappa)^{-1},$$
using $i_0^*a^*C=C$. This is precisely the displayed formula in the statement under its stipulated fibre identifications. Once a normalized comparison is supplied, isIso_specialization follows directly from the isomorphism of atZero proved in lines_and_fibres and the displayed composite defining specialization.

source.place: Gluing, second paragraph and final specialization

proof.text:
We verify the compatibility of the fibre identifications with successive base changes, before using uniqueness. Write $b_{h,v}:v_X^*\omega_h\to\omega_{h_v}$ for the canonical exceptional comparison, obtained by taking the right-adjoint mate of the inverse compact-support exchange. The ordinary unbounded compact-support exchange is compatible with composite changes of base. Mate pasting therefore gives, under the inverse-image compositors,
$$b_{h,vw}=b_{h_v,w}\circ w_X^*b_{h,v}.$$
For $v:S'\to S$, put $\bar v:\mathbf A^1_{S'}\to\mathbf A^1_S$, and write $b_C:v^*C\to C'$, $b_F:\bar v^*F\to F'$, and $b_N:v^*(z^*\omega_\pi)\to z'^*\omega_{\pi'}$ for the section pullbacks of these maps. Apply the preceding pasting identity to the commuting rectangle $\bar v i'_r=i_rv$, in its two decompositions (first $\bar v$ then $i'_r$, or first $i_r$ then $v$). The centre/fibre identifications of Step 4 give the same Cartesian diagram in both decompositions. Pulling its mates to the section gives the explicit equalities
$$\theta'\circ i_1'^*b_F=b_C\circ v^*\theta,\qquad
\eta'\circ i_0'^*b_F=b_N\circ v^*\eta.$$
This is the required compatibility with the fibre maps; exactness of inverse image alone would not establish it.

source.place: Final base-change paragraph, expanded by canonical compact-support exchange and mate pasting; Stacks 0F7L/lemma-base-change-shriek, 0E46 and 0E47

proof.text:
All these $b$ maps are isomorphisms by smooth base change. The pullback candidate for the normalized comparison over $S'$ is explicitly
$$\kappa^v=a'^*b_C\circ\bar v^*\kappa\circ b_F^{-1}:F'\longrightarrow a'^*C'.$$
By the first equality in Step 11 its restriction at $1$ is $b_C\circ v^*\theta\circ(i_1'^*b_F)^{-1}=\theta'$. It is thus the normalized comparison $\kappa'$ by Step 9's uniqueness, which applies over every such Noetherian $S'$ (Steps 3--4 preserve the deformation hypotheses, and compactifiability is assumed). At $0$, substituting the second equality of Step 11 and inverting $i_0'^*\kappa^v$ gives
$$\delta'\circ b_C=b_N\circ v^*\delta.$$
These are exactly the claimed base-change identities for $\kappa$ and $\delta$. For the empty base every sheaf map and diagram is unique; in rank zero all the polynomial and monomial calculations above have no $x_j$ and reduce to $B/I=R$, so no case was excluded.

Separatedness of the centre map and the base-changed structural map.
The generic prime makes the geometric affine line irreducible.
A sheaf with zero geometric stalks is zero, so the local maps agree.
The image of the difference of maps has stalks equal to the images of the stalk maps.
